title: Linking through unique student identifier
description: The flow contains student id which is a unique identifier that can be used to link data across the system, connecting submission and grading activities to specific students.
assumptions: Student id is unique within the system context

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The system processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Student id directly identifies individual students

title: Unique identifier in data flow
description: The data contains student id which is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, enabling direct identification.
assumptions: Student id is a unique identifier for each student

title: Attributable submission data
description: Submission and grading request data can be used to prevent a student from denying their submission or grading requests, creating non-repudiation evidence.
assumptions: Data is logged and can be attributed to specific students

title: Sensitive data types in flow
description: Student id, course information, and file references may be considered sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required.
assumptions: Student identifiers and course data are considered personal data

title: Data propagation to grading service
description: Personal data is propagated to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2) where it may be accessible beyond what is functionally necessary for the specific request.
assumptions: P2 may retain or use data beyond immediate processing needs

title: Student unawareness of data transfer
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data is being transferred between the Portal Web App and the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not explicitly detail this internal data flow

title: Lack of student control over data processing
description: Students may lack control over how their submission and grading data is processed and transferred between these services.
assumptions: No explicit consent or preference mechanism for this data flow

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: The flow may process more personal data than necessary if all fields (student id, course, file reference, requesting role) are not all required for the grading service function.
assumptions: Some data fields may be redundant for the specific processing purpose
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether all data fields are functionally necessary

title: Processing of identified teacher data
description: The teacher's identity is explicitly processed during login and when requesting submission queues. The system processes identified data about the teacher including their identity, courses taught, and access patterns.
assumptions: Teacher authentication requires identification

title: Identifier in submission queue data
description: The submission queue likely contains student identifiers (names, IDs) that uniquely reference the identity of data subjects (students). This identifiable information is processed when the teacher requests the queue.
assumptions: Submission queues contain student identifying information

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: Teacher and student identifiers in the submission queue allow linking of data to specific individuals. The system can link submission data to both the reviewing teacher and the submitting students.
assumptions: System uses unique identifiers for teachers and students

title: Profiling teacher through review patterns
description: The system can analyze the teacher's review patterns, courses taught, and submission access to create a profile of the teacher's activities and preferences.
assumptions: System logs teacher access and review activities

title: Sensitive student data in submission queue
description: The submission queue may contain sensitive student data (grades, work, personal information) that is more sensitive than functionally required for the teacher to simply see what needs review.
assumptions: Submissions contain student work and potentially sensitive information

title: Implicit disclosure of teacher-course relationships
description: By requesting the submission queue, the teacher implicitly discloses which courses they teach and are responsible for reviewing, which may not be necessary for the core functionality.
assumptions: Queue request reveals course assignments

title: Attributable teacher actions
description: The teacher's login and queue request can be attributed to them through authentication logs, preventing them from denying they accessed the submission queue.
assumptions: System maintains authentication and access logs

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students whose submissions are in the queue may not be aware that their data is being accessed and processed by teachers, or when this occurs.
assumptions: Students are not notified when teachers access their submissions

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: The system may process more student data than necessary for the teacher to review submissions, potentially violating GDPR data minimization principles.
assumptions: Full submission data is exposed rather than minimal required data
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data exposure in the queue

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The portal processes and displays student names, which are directly identified personal data. This is inherent to the functionality of showing submissions to teachers.
assumptions: Student names are considered personal data under privacy regulations

title: Student names as direct identifiers
description: Student names serve as unique references to the identity of data subjects, allowing direct identification of which student submitted which work.
assumptions: Student names are unique within the school context

title: Profiling students through submission patterns
description: Teachers can analyze student submissions over time to profile individual students based on work quality, submission timing patterns, and content characteristics.
assumptions: Multiple submissions are visible over time, enabling pattern analysis

title: Attributable submission evidence
description: Student submissions with timestamps can be used to attribute work to specific students, preventing them from denying they submitted particular work.
assumptions: Submission records are maintained with student identification

title: Sensitive work content disclosure
description: Student work content may include sensitive personal information (personal essays, creative work, health-related assignments) that exceeds what is functionally necessary for grading.
assumptions: Some student work may contain sensitive personal information
uncertainty_note: Depends on the nature of assignments in the curriculum

title: Fine-grained individual submission disclosure
description: Personal data is disclosed at the individual student level with specific work content and submission times, which is more granular than might be needed for some grading purposes.
assumptions: Some grading could potentially be done with less granular data

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of how their submissions are displayed to teachers, including what information is visible and for how long it is retained.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain the data flow to teachers

title: Lack of student control over submission display
description: Students likely have no ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their work is displayed to teachers or what information is shown.
assumptions: The system does not provide student preference controls for submission visibility

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Students may lack adequate controls to exercise their data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) regarding their submission data displayed to teachers.
assumptions: The system may not provide mechanisms for students to manage their submission data
uncertainty_note: Depends on system implementation of data subject rights

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: The flow contains student id and grader id which are unique identifiers that can be used to link this grading data to specific individuals across the system and potentially with other data sources.
assumptions: Student id and grader id are unique identifiers within the system

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes identified data including student id, grader id, grade, and feedback text. This is explicit identified information about both the student (data subject) and teacher (data processor).
assumptions: Student id and grader id directly identify individuals

title: Identifier in data
description: The data contains unique references to the identity of the data subject (student id) and the grader (grader id), making both parties directly identifiable from this data flow.
assumptions: Student id and grader id are unique identifiers

title: Attributable data evidence
description: The grade and feedback data submitted by the teacher can be used to attribute this action to the specific teacher (via grader id), preventing them from denying they submitted this grading information.
assumptions: Grader id is logged and associated with the submission

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Grades and written feedback are sensitive educational data that reveal information about a student's academic performance. This data should only be collected when strictly required for the grading functionality.
assumptions: Grades and feedback are considered sensitive educational data

title: Data retention duration
description: The grades and feedback data may be retained longer than functionally needed. Without clear retention policies, this data could be kept indefinitely, increasing privacy risks.
assumptions: Retention period is not specified in the flow description
uncertainty_note: Retention policy not specified in flow description

title: Student unawareness of processing
description: Students (data subjects) may not be aware that their grades and feedback are being processed, stored, and potentially shared through this system. They may not know what data is collected or how it's used.
assumptions: Students are not explicitly informed about grading data processing
uncertainty_note: Assuming no explicit notification mechanism is in place

title: Lack of data subject preferences control
description: Students may lack control over how their grading data (grades, feedback) is processed, stored, or shared. They may not be able to set preferences or provide consent for this processing.
assumptions: No preference or consent mechanism is described for students
uncertainty_note: Assuming no consent mechanism is in place

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: The system may lack adequate support for GDPR data subject rights such as access, rectification, erasure, and portability for students regarding their grading data.
assumptions: No data subject rights mechanisms are described in the flow
uncertainty_note: Assuming no explicit data subject rights implementation

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than necessary. For example, the feedback text might contain more detail than functionally required, or data might be retained longer than needed.
assumptions: Data minimization practices are not explicitly described
uncertainty_note: Cannot confirm without knowing functional requirements

title: Grades and feedback disclosed to predetermined student
description: The portal sends grades and teacher feedback to the student. While this is the intended recipient, the data is personal and sensitive academic information. The threat is that this data is made accessible to a specific party (the student) which, while necessary for functionality, represents a disclosure of personal data that must be properly secured and limited to only the intended recipient.
assumptions: The student is authenticated and authorized to view their own grades

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The portal processes and displays identified data (grades and feedback) tied to a specific student's identity. The system must correctly associate the data with the right student and ensure only that student can access it.
assumptions: Student authentication is in place to ensure correct data association

title: Observed communications of grades and feedback
description: The communication of grades and feedback from the portal to the student could be observed by unauthorized parties if the transmission is not properly secured (e.g., via network interception).
assumptions: Transmission security depends on implementation (HTTPS, etc.)
uncertainty_note: Depends on implementation details not provided in flow description

title: Student access control to their own data
description: While the student is accessing their own data, there may be limitations on their ability to access, view, or control how their grades and feedback are displayed or stored in the portal.
assumptions: Portal provides standard access mechanisms for students
uncertainty_note: Depends on portal implementation features

title: Parent-child account linking through unique identifiers
description: The Grades Portal Web App maintains links between parent accounts and child accounts using unique identifiers. This creates a linking threat where the system can associate parent access patterns with specific children's data.
assumptions: Parent and child accounts are linked through unique identifiers in the system

title: Processing of identified parent and child data
description: The system processes identified data including parent login credentials, parent identity, child identity, and child grades. All data subjects are identified rather than anonymized.
assumptions: The system requires parent authentication and processes identifiable child data

title: Attributable grade access evidence
description: The system creates data records that attribute grade access to specific parent accounts, preventing the parent from denying they accessed their child's grades.
assumptions: The system logs parent access to grades with authentication records

title: Sensitive educational data disclosure
description: Grades are sensitive educational data that may be perceived as highly sensitive. The system discloses this data to parents, which requires careful consideration of data type sensitivity.
assumptions: Grades are considered sensitive personal data under applicable regulations

title: Implicit data disclosure through grade access
description: When parents access grades, the system may implicitly disclose additional information such as which courses the child is enrolled in, performance patterns over time, or comparison data with other students.
assumptions: Grade data includes contextual information beyond raw scores
uncertainty_note: Depends on what additional data is included in grade responses

title: Child unawareness of grade data processing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their grade data is being accessed and processed by their parent through the system, especially if the child is a minor.
assumptions: The child may not have visibility into parent access to their grades
uncertainty_note: Depends on age of child and notification mechanisms in place

title: Child lack of control over grade data sharing
description: The child may lack control over preferences for how their grade data is shared with parents, including what data is shared and when.
assumptions: The system does not provide children with consent or preference controls for parent access
uncertainty_note: Depends on system design and age of data subjects

title: Insufficient data subject controls for child
description: The child as data subject may lack adequate controls over their personal data (grades), including rights to access, rectify, or object to processing, which could violate GDPR or similar regulations.
assumptions: Applicable regulations grant data subject rights to children
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and age of child

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The Grades Portal processes and transmits identified personal data (child's grades, feedback, submission history) that is directly linked to the child's identity. This data is explicitly identified rather than anonymized.
assumptions: The portal maintains and transmits data that can be directly associated with specific children

title: Revealing attributes in academic data
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject. Academic performance patterns can be distinctive and identifying.
assumptions: Academic data contains attributes that can help identify or distinguish the child

title: Quasi-identifier combination in academic records
description: The combination of grades, feedback, and submission history across subjects and time periods can serve as a quasi-identifier, allowing linking of data to a specific child even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Multiple data points about academic performance are combined and transmitted

title: Sensitive academic data disclosure
description: Grades and academic feedback are sensitive personal data types that should only be disclosed when strictly required. The portal displays this data to parents, which may exceed functional necessity in some contexts.
assumptions: Academic performance data is considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Excessive granularity of academic data
description: The portal may disclose personal data at a more fine-grained level than needed (e.g., detailed feedback, specific submission history) beyond what is functionally required for parental oversight.
assumptions: The level of detail in grades and feedback may exceed what parents need to know
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about the actual granularity of data displayed

title: Child unaware of data processing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their grades, feedback, and submission history are being processed and disclosed to parents through the portal.
assumptions: Children may not be informed about what academic data is shared with parents

title: Lack of child control over data sharing preferences
description: The child may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their academic data is processed and shared with parents through the portal.
assumptions: Children typically have limited control over academic data sharing in school systems

title: Insufficient data subject controls for child
description: The system may lack adequate support for data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) for the child whose academic data is being processed and shared.
assumptions: Children's data subject rights may not be fully implemented in the portal
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about the specific implementation of data subject rights

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (detailed grades, feedback, submission history) may be processed and shared than is actually needed for the functional purpose of parental oversight.
assumptions: The scope of data shared may exceed what is minimally necessary
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about the actual data minimization practices

title: Linking through unique account identifiers
description: The account directory stores account records with unique identifiers. When the grading service writes parent-child relationship links, these can be linked through the unique account identifiers, enabling correlation of grading data with specific individuals.
assumptions: Account directory uses unique identifiers for accounts

title: Linking through quasi-identifiers from parent-child relationships
description: Parent-child relationship links combined with other account attributes can serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling re-identification of individuals even if direct identifiers are removed.
assumptions: Parent-child relationships are stored as structured data in the account directory

title: Processing of identified data in grading service
description: The grading service processes identified data (account records with parent-child relationships) when writing to the account directory, directly handling personally identifiable information.
assumptions: Account records contain personally identifiable information

title: Revealing attributes in parent-child relationship data
description: Parent-child relationship links are revealing attributes that support identification of data subjects, as they expose family structures and relationships.
assumptions: Parent-child relationships are considered revealing personal attributes

title: Sensitive data type - parent-child relationships
description: Parent-child relationship data is highly sensitive personal information that should only be collected when strictly required. The necessity of storing this in the account directory should be evaluated.
assumptions: Parent-child relationships are considered sensitive personal data

title: Data retention in account directory
description: Account records and parent-child relationships stored in the data store may be retained longer than functionally needed for grading purposes, creating unnecessary privacy risk.
assumptions: Data retention policies may not align with functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about actual retention policies

title: Unawareness of parent-child relationship processing
description: Parents and students may not be aware that their relationship data is being collected, stored, and linked in the account directory by the grading service.
assumptions: Data subjects may not have been informed about this specific data processing

title: Lack of control over relationship data rectification
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify incorrect parent-child relationship data or request erasure of this information from the account directory.
assumptions: Data subject rights mechanisms may not cover relationship data

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing parent-child relationship links in the account directory may process more personal data than actually needed for the grading functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Parent-child relationships may not be strictly necessary for grading operations
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual functional requirements of the system

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service processes and transmits identified student data including grade records, assignments, and account directory information to the cloud hosting provider.
assumptions: Account directory contains student identifiers and grade records are linked to specific students

title: Storage of student identifiers in cloud
description: The cloud hosting provider receives and stores data containing unique references to student identities through the account directory and grade records.
assumptions: Account directory contains unique student identifiers

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: Student data can be linked across systems using unique identifiers present in the account directory and grade records transmitted to the cloud provider.
assumptions: Unique student identifiers are present in the transmitted data

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are shared with the cloud hosting provider, a predetermined external party, potentially exceeding what is functionally necessary.
assumptions: Cloud hosting provider is a known, predetermined party

title: Excessive volume of personal data in backup
description: Nightly database backup ships full grade records and account directory, potentially including more data than functionally required for backup purposes.
assumptions: Full database backup includes all student data without filtering

title: Student unawareness of cloud data processing
description: Students may be unaware that their grade records and account information are being processed and stored by a third-party cloud hosting provider.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly disclose cloud backup practices
uncertainty_note: Depends on institutional privacy policy transparency

title: Lack of student control over backup data
description: Students likely have no control over rectification or erasure of their data in cloud backups, which may be retained for extended periods.
assumptions: Backup retention policies are not student-controllable

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Transmitting full database backups to cloud provider may violate GDPR data minimization if all data is not strictly necessary for the backup function.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply to student data
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific data handling practices
